text:
Alex M: quick summary from the nsys run on the weekend: looks like kernel_selector is picking the int8 path for short sequences on A100 and that's causing a ~12-15% tail regression for batch sizes <= 4. attached timeline shows many tiny kernels chained together.

Maria P: ugh. do you have the timeline snippet? can you paste the command you ran?

Alex M: ran: `nsys profile --output=run1 --trace=cuda,osrt --sample=none --capture-range=cuda:kernel` then opened in Nsight. the hot area is around the "kernel_select_and_dispatch" call. sample from the report: 
```
# timeline top kernels
kernel_select_and_dispatch  42.1ms
matmul_int8_kernel         5.8ms  x 7
matmul_fp16_fused          3.2ms  x 2
kv_cache_lookup            12.4ms
```

Sam R: so kernel_select is doing heavy work at runtime. are we running the selector per request or per batch?

Alex M: per-batch, but we recompute a lot of heuristics (seq_len distribution, quantized flag, cached_kv hit ratio) that include scanning the batch. cheap when batch is big, expensive when bs<=4.

Devon K: my 2c: instrumenting more doesn't always help. if we add a ton of NVTX ranges around every small helper we might increase overhead and obscure the timeline with noise. i'd prefer coarse-grained ranges for now (per-request + per-kernel-dispatch) and add sampling for small/fast requests.

Ying Z: agreed on sampling. also we should standardize our range names so they are parseable by the trace postprocessor. proposal: `req=<req_id>|phase=<phase>|sel=<selector_tag>|bs=<batch_size>|ql=<quant>` as the NVTX string. it encodes the important bits without adding separate metadata channels.

Maria P: that name is long but machine-friendly. downside: NVTX name is a single string, so parsers need to split on `|`. ok for tooling. question: do we include shard/gpu index?

Sam R: include gpu index only for cross-GPU aggregation. i'd rather we keep per-GPU traces lean and add the device id from nsight metadata.

Alex M: also spotted double-instrumentation: we already wrap the high-level request span in the request middleware. then kernel_selector adds its own ranges. that's fine if we keep them distinct: `REQ/<id>` vs `SEL/<...>`. but don't duplicate for tiny helper functions.

Devon K: actionable checklist:
- keep top-level request span: `REQ/<short-id>` (owner: Alex)
- add one NVTX range around kernel_selector decision block annotated with selector string (owner: Sam)
- add NVTX around batching boundary (owner: Maria)
- enable sampling: only instrument requests with latency > 8ms or random 1/1000 flag (owner: Ying)

Ying Z: sample instrumentation snippet (pseudo):
```
if (should_sample(req)) {
  nvtxRangePushA(name.c_str());
  // heavy work
  nvtxRangePop();
}
```
where should_sample = (req.latency_est>8ms) || (rng() % 1000 == 7)

Sam R: question: can we annotate the selector output with a short enum instead of full kernel name? e.g. `SEL=I8_V1` or `SEL=F16_FUSED` to keep name lengths down.

Alex M: yes, map full kernel id -> short tag at compile time. we'll keep a lookup in the runtime for trace rendering. also add a debug mode that expands tags for dev builds.

Maria P: perf-bot: can you log the perf counters for the next run (L2 hit, DRAM bw) and attach to the trace?

perf-bot: scheduled: next nightly profiling job will include counters: l2_hit_rate, dram_bw, sm_utilization. attaching to /artifacts/prof/run-nightly-180012.

Devon K: one more: avoid NVTX in the inner kv-cache hot loops. instead add an aggregated counter when multiple cache ops exceed X per request. NVTX overhead in microloops kills throughput.

Ying Z: I'll push a small PR with the naming util and sampling gate. PR will include a sample parser in tools/trace that converts `|` delimited names into JSON for dashboards.

Alex M: thanks team. plan: land lightweight NVTX changes (REQ + SEL + BATCH) behind a flag, run nightly with perf counters, review results Tuesday. if we still see selector mispicks, we'll consider moving part of the selector offline (cache decisions for known model shapes). :thumbsup:

Sam R: sounds good. cc @eng-sre for potential increase in storage for traces when sampling is off.

Maria P: noted. I'll update the runbook with instrumentation toggles and the naming convention.

Alex M: end of thread: attaching a screenshot of the nsys flame view to the ticket (not in slack).
